_readme: Target spec per asset group. See docs/art_spec.md. Globs are POSIX-style, relative to the repo root. 'fit' is one of: scale_canvas (resize the whole canvas; use for animation frame sets so frames stay aligned), trim_pad (trim to content, scale to fit, re-pad; use for standalone props), keep (palette only, no geometry change). 'anchor' is center or bottom. 'ramp' optionally restricts the palette to one ramp plus INK. 'conform: false' means audit it but never rewrite it.

groups.name: generated_enemies
groups.note: Gemini output, 1408x768 JPEG on a magenta field. MUST precede the 'enemies' group, which is fit:keep and would leave these at full size. key_tolerance is high because JPEG ringing makes the 'flat' magenta noisy at the subject edge. Excludes the VIOLET ramp: the magenta key leaves a blended rim on the outer silhouette that otherwise snaps to VIOLET, giving every sprite a purple halo. VIOLET is reserved for boss/cursed/rare (art_spec.md section 3), so no prop or enemy texture should reach for it anyway.

groups.name: generated_props
groups.note: Roughly square props, 2x2 tiles. anchor:bottom so they stand on their cell instead of floating -- DungeonDecorator relies on the art's base sitting at the canvas bottom. Excludes the VIOLET ramp: the magenta key leaves a blended rim on the outer silhouette that otherwise snaps to VIOLET, giving every sprite a purple halo. VIOLET is reserved for boss/cursed/rare (art_spec.md section 3), so no prop or enemy texture should reach for it anyway.

groups.name: generated_props_tall
groups.note: Tall props, 2x3 tiles. freezer_door.png is the middle door cropped out of a 3-variant sheet the model returned. Excludes the VIOLET ramp: the magenta key leaves a blended rim on the outer silhouette that otherwise snaps to VIOLET, giving every sprite a purple halo. VIOLET is reserved for boss/cursed/rare (art_spec.md section 3), so no prop or enemy texture should reach for it anyway.

groups.name: generated_props_wide
groups.note: Wide prop, 3x2 tiles -- content aspect was 1.88, so a 32x32 canvas would have shrunk it to half height. Excludes the VIOLET ramp: the magenta key leaves a blended rim on the outer silhouette that otherwise snaps to VIOLET, giving every sprite a purple halo. VIOLET is reserved for boss/cursed/rare (art_spec.md section 3), so no prop or enemy texture should reach for it anyway.

groups.name: staging
groups.note: AUDIT ONLY. Raw generator handoff plus contact sheets. Carries a .gdignore so Godot does not import it. The full-res masters now live in assets/_source/, so this folder is safe to delete once the art is wired in.

groups.name: player_anim
groups.note: 112 frames, 8 directions. scale_canvas (never trim) so frames stay aligned. The old net scale was 1.5 * 0.25 = 0.375: 68px of art crushed onto 25.5 world px at 1.12 screen px per texel. 24x24 would preserve that size exactly but the face falls apart; 32x32 costs a 25% size increase and keeps the character readable next to 48px enemies. Sprite scale becomes 1.0 and hitboxes are unchanged.

groups.name: player_portrait
groups.note: Menu chrome, not world-space -- palette only, size left alone. NOTE: main_menu.tscn draws it at custom_minimum_size 180px tall from a 160px source, i.e. 1.125x, which is off the pixel grid. Setting that to 160 makes it exact. Left alone here because it is a UI layout change, not an art change.

groups.name: player_bullet
groups.note: Golden drumstick. READABILITY: this reads almost identically to the enemy flame bullet mid-fight. To force it cool, add "ramp": "COOL" here -- but that costs the chicken theme, so an INK+COOL_3 rim is probably the better fix. Design call, left to you.

groups.name: enemy_bullets
groups.note: Single-subject sprites, so a detached fragment under 15% of the main blob is safely noise. lettuce.png carries a stray 33px grey bar below the sprite (10.8% of the subject) that would otherwise land in the content bbox and shove the sprite off-centre when re-padded.

groups.name: enemies
groups.note: Already on grid at scale 1.0. Palette only. Bosses reuse these at integer scale 2.

groups.name: decorations
groups.note: 32x32 and 32x40, placed at scale 1.0 on integer tile positions by dungeon_decorator.gd. Geometry is already correct; resizing would shift their centres. Palette only.

groups.name: obstacles
groups.note: 32x48 / 32x40 at scale 1.0. Palette only.

groups.name: dungeon_props
groups.note: 64x48 and 32x48 at scale 1.0. Palette only.

groups.name: spawn_indicator
groups.note: Was 256x256 at scale 0.3 -- 0.9 screen px per texel, i.e. sub-pixel, detail thrown away entirely. 5268 colours.

groups.name: portal
groups.note: 3 animation frames -- scale_canvas keeps them aligned. Was 192x236 at scale 0.35, ~19k colours (not pixel art).

groups.name: egg_blade
groups.note: Orbiting blade ability. Was 125x125 at scale 0.3, 1886 colours.

groups.name: sodas
groups.note: 32x32, already on grid. Palette only.

groups.name: shop_icons
groups.note: 70 files at 128x128 with 4.5k-11.7k colours -- smooth painterly AI images, the single biggest style break in the game. shop_ui.tscn shows them at 160px with KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED, so 32x32 lands on an exact 5x integer zoom.

groups.name: kitchen_tileset
groups.note: GENERATED, never conformed -- tools/make_kitchen_tileset.py draws it and is the single source of truth. Running conform on it would copy it into assets/_source/ and create a second, stale master. It is palette-perfect and seam-checked by construction; re-run the generator with --check after editing it. 160x160 atlas of 16x16 tiles; only 37 cells are used, the 6x6 block at (0,0)-(5,5) plus SOLID_ROCK at (8,7), a layout dictated by scenes/dungeon/dungeon_renderer.gd.

groups.name: old_tileset
groups.glob: assets/2D Pixel Dungeon Asset Pack/New_tilemap.png,assets/2D Pixel Dungeon Asset Pack/Kitchen_tilemap.png
groups.note: AUDIT ONLY. Superseded by kitchen_tileset.png and no longer referenced by any scene. Safe to delete along with the rest of the dungeon pack.

groups.name: ui
groups.note: AUDIT ONLY, never rewritten. Menu buttons are 210x55 with 7k+ colours and baked-in text; the logo is 39k colours; panel.png is 9-sliced. Quantising these to 40 colours would wreck the text and the 9-slice borders, and their sizes are coupled to Control layout. Restyling the UI is a separate pass. GUI_4x.png (153 colours) is the one genuinely pixel-art file here.

groups.name: unused_pack
groups.note: AUDIT ONLY. ~180 files from the free pack, almost all unreferenced. Not worth conforming; delete when the kitchen tileset lands.

groups.name: unreferenced
groups.note: AUDIT ONLY. Nothing in scenes/, scripts/ or resources/ references these -- 374 status-effect frames, the spare bullet sheet, the crosshair and the superseded player_idle.png. Conforming dead weight is wasted effort; wire them up (then move them into a real group) or delete them.
